question.text: In response to the famine, the UK repealed these laws, which imposed tariffs on imported grains, not a vegetable with yellow kernels as the name would suggest.
question.clue: Benjamin Disraeli was one of the most vocal supporters of these laws, which were repealed by Sir Robert Peel and the opposing Whigs in 1849.

swap.text: The Magna Carta created the first modern form of this English governing body, which in modern times is made up of the House of Lord and House of Commons.
swap.answerHtml: English Parliament (accept Parliament of England; accept Parliament of the United Kingdom)
swap.clue: The "Long" iteration of this group followed its "Rump" iteration.

question.text: The Frame-Breaking Act was passed in response to these protesters who attempted to destroy industrial machinery.
question.clue: Like the Swing Riots, this movement was inspired by a mythological king or general.

swap.text: Earlier, this ruler successfully repelled a Viking invasion of England. He is the only English ruler with the epithet "The Great."
swap.clue: A daughter of this ruler extended a defense system in which thirty fortresses were garrisoned by four men to each wall perch; that system of burhs was detailed in the Burghal Hidage during the reign of this ruler's son, Edward the Elder.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Christmas in British history.
question.text: Celebrating Christmas was banned during the rule of this man, who served as Lord Protector after Charles I was executed at the end of the English Civil War.
question.clue: This man's sieges of Wexford and Drogheda were followed by massacres of Irish civilians.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Levellers, an English Civil War radical group.
swap.text: Opponents to the radical ideas of the Levellers included the commanders of this parliamentarian military force, which included Thomas Fairfax and Oliver Cromwell.
swap.clue: This organization was the source of the Coldstream Guards and the Blues and Royals, and certain people were not allowed to join it according to the Self-Denying Ordinance.

question.leadin: Answer the following about things that happened in 1979.
question.text: This Tory politician became the United Kingdom's Prime Minister, ushering in new neoliberal programs of free trade and reduced public spending. This prime minister controversially abolished free milk for school children.
question.clue: The defeat of the first Scottish devolution referendum led to the vote of no confidence against James Callaghan ("KAL-uh-han") that triggered this person's election.

swap.leadin: The night before this event began, the Santisima Ferdinand covertly landed at Mullet Creek.
swap.text: Name this brief 1982 war fought over the namesake British archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean. Military engagements during this war include the Battle of Goose Green and the sinking of the General Belgrano cruiser.
swap.answerHtml: Falklands War (or Falkland Islands War; accept South Atlantic War)
swap.clue: This conflict began when one side's troops landed on April 2, and ended when they were forced to give up the territorial capital of Port Stanley in mid-June of the same year.

question.leadin: Identify these important liberalizing documents in European history.
question.text: With his seal affixed on June 15, 1215, King John conceded to this document proclaiming the rights of the barons.
question.clue: This document prohibited the king from levying scutage without consent, and it codifies the use of habeas corpus in common law.

swap.text: The RAF defeated the Luftwaffe on Eagle Day during this aerial "battle" fought over a namesake country, ending German hopes of launching Operation Sea Lion.
swap.clue: This battle, intended as a precursor to Operation Sea Lion, included the "never was so much owed by so many" speech.

question.text: James MacLaine wrote a letter of apology after robbing a man with this surname. Another man with this surname who was criticised by Henry Fielding for his corruption served as the first British Prime Minister..

swap.leadin: A Soviet competitor to this aircraft, the Tupolev Tu-144, retired its passenger flights after less than a year.
swap.text: Name this commercial aircraft developed by the British Aircraft Corporation and Sud Aviation that was used for transatlantic supersonic commercial flights.
swap.clue: This plane developed jointly by Air France and British Airways, which faced airspace restrictions in several countries after residents complained about the excessive noise that it caused.

question.leadin: A crisis caused by the loss of resources led royals to reform the use of these locations in response to the Holznot ("HOLTZ-note").
question.text: Name these places that included the ancient Hercynian version. One of these places named for Dean had a portion reserved for royals.
question.answerHtml: forest [accept Royal Forests; accept Forest of Dean; accept Hercynian Forest]
question.clue: Germanic tribesmen under the command of Arminius won a battle named after the Teutoberg type of this location.

swap.text: The first English Bible to be printed was the Great Bible supervised by this sometime bishop of Exeter, who frequently found himself exiled from England due to his Puritanism.

question.leadin: Rædwald of East Anglia was unusual in being described with this title because most others who were given it came from the major kingdoms of Wessex, Mercia or Northumbria.
question.text: Give this original-language title, used in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle for eight rulers who achieved a semblance of hegemony over the other rulers of the Heptarchy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Falklands War.
swap.text: Guardsman Simon Weston suffered severe burns after this ship was bombed at Bluff Cove.

question.leadin: Answer the following about incorrect predictions based on the Book of Revelation in early modern Britain.
question.text: In the 1590s, this Scottish scholar calculated from Revelation that the Apocalypse would happen either in 1688 or in 1700. This scholar introduced a multiplication technique called his namesake "bones."
question.answerHtml: John Napier of Merchiston [or Ioannes Neper; accept Napier’s rods or Napier’s bones]

swap.text: Kenneth moved his capital from Dunadd to this site in Perthshire. A stone named for this village is used for the coronation of Scottish monarchs.

question.leadin: His major work was compiled by Richard Hosley.
question.text: Name this medieval writer and historian whose namesake chronicles were used by William Shakespeare to write Cymbeline, Macbeth and other plays.

swap.leadin: Identify these figures associated with William the Conqueror, FTPE.
swap.text: One of William's closest advisers was this Lombard Archbishop of Canterbury who was instrumental in securing Papal approval for the invasion of England, and foiled the plot of the Earls of Norfolk and Hereford.
